abstract: Social media platforms have traditionally relied on internal moderation teams and partnerships with independent fact-checking organizations to identify and flag problematic content. Recently, however, platforms including X (formerly Twitter) and Meta have shifted toward community-driven content moderation by launching their own versions of crowd-sourced fact-checking-Community Notes. If effectively scaled and governed, such crowd-checking initiatives have the potential to combat misinformation as successfully as community-driven efforts once did with spam. However, moderating misinformation is inherently more complex: perceptions of truth are often shaped by personal biases, political leanings, and cultural contexts, complicating consensus on what constitutes misleading content. This suggests that community efforts, while valuable, cannot replace the indispensable role of professional fact-checkers. Here we explore the emerging role of community-driven moderation, critically evaluate both the promises and the challenges of Community Notes at scale, and identify how collaborative and technical innovations can integrate the two distinct approaches.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Promises and pitfalls of community moderation on social media

abstract: India routinely experiences some of the highest concentrations of fine particulate matter (PM 2.5) air pollution in the world. Although India’s population predominantly lives in rural areas and smaller cities, policy efforts to date have emphasized air pollution in India’s large cities. In contrast, there is limited understanding of air pollutant dynamics in India’s rural and less urbanized areas. Here, we established a well-calibrated lower-cost PM 2.5 sensor network spanning a wide range of urbanicity (population densities: 300 to 30,000 people/km 2) outside and inside of Delhi. The network of 49 sites incorporated a 160 km measurement transect to capture ambient PM 2.5 trends of the Delhi megacity, as well as stratified measurements in villages, small cities, and Delhi itself. We report on data from 5 mo of operation (July–November 2024) spanning the cleanest and most polluted times of the year. PM 2.5 concentrations at rural sites consistently exceeded those at urban sites by about 20% during every month of our study. Analysis of diurnal PM 2.5 cycles showed sharp morning (approximately 06:00–10:00 LT) and evening (approximately 16:00–20:00 LT) concentration peaks at rural sites that were absent at urban sites. We attribute these events to widespread use of solid fuels for cooking, heating, and small-scale industry in suburban and rural settings. These striking enhancements in rural air pollution are missed by satellite remote sensing data, and our findings run contrary to the general societal perception that Indian cities are pollution hotspots relative to rural areas.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Rural outdoor air pollution exceeds urban levels in the Delhi megacity region

abstract: The renewed increase of methane (CH 4) in the atmosphere since 2007 is an imminent threat to the stability of the climate system and undermines climate policy goals. A reversal in the trend of its carbon isotopic composition (δ 13 C CH4) in the 21st century indicates a fundamental shift in the global CH 4 cycle. Here, we investigate the origin of this δ 13 C CH4 trend by determining isotope source signatures of CH 4 emissions based on high and mid-northern latitude observations. A clear latitude gradient and seasonal cycle of the source signatures reflect the spatially and temporally varying contributions of the different sources, each with distinct signatures. We find a large shift in the source signature after 2007 between −3.6 and −5.1‰ at high northern latitudes, and a moderate change between −0.4 and −0.9‰ at mid-northern latitudes. The decrease in δ 13 C CH4 source signature is likely caused by a shift from thermogenic and pyrogenic to microbial sources, accompanied by a likely decrease in the isotopic signature of the microbial emissions, possibly resulting from climate change. Our results suggest that current inverse models may underestimate the shift between fossil and microbial emissions at high northern latitudes, or that microbial methanogenesis pathways change much more strongly than currently believed. Source changes at high latitudes have a disproportionate contribution to the observed trend in atmospheric δ 13 C CH4.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Isotope evidence for changing methane sources at high northern latitudes

abstract: Proper meiotic homolog pairing requires the coordination of two processes: DNA recombination and chromosome-scale mechanical movements. Here, we identify a dual role in both meiotic processes for the chromatin reader ZCWPW1 in mouse spermatocytes. The current dogma proposes that ZCWPW1 acts downstream of PRDM9, reading the PRDM9-deposited H3K4 and K36me3 modifications at recombination hotspots and promoting DSB repair. Using superresolution imaging, we show that ZCWPW1 is diffuse throughout the nucleus but enriched at the nuclear periphery near TRF1, LINC complex components, and dynein. ZCWPW1 CUT&RUN further confirms its genomic enrichment at subtelomeric regions. Loss of ZCWPW1 disrupts telomere architecture, weakens telomere-LINC-motor coupling, and markedly reduces chromosome movement. These defects are more severe than, and mechanistically independent of, those observed in Prdm9 −/− spermatocytes. Together, our data reveal an unexpected PRDM9-independent role for ZCWPW1 as an intranuclear regulator of both recombination and mechanical movements that coordinate to drive efficient homolog pairing.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: ZCWPW1 organizes telomeric architecture to drive meiotic chromosome movements

abstract: This study employs a set of behavioral experiments to examine how individuals perceive the humanness of social media posts about the 2024 U.S. presidential debate between Kamala Harris and Donald Trump. Posts presented in the experiment were authored either by humans or chatbots, varying the large language model (LLM), the model architecture, the social media platform, and the political personas. Participants judged randomly paired posts to identify which they perceived to be AI-generated. We find that human-authored posts were on average perceived as more human-like than AI outputs generated from five of the six LLMs in this study. However, participants' ability to detect AI-generated content is limited. They do so only slightly above chance in human-AI pairs, and this ability weakens for newer LLMs, varies by platform, and reflects partisan bias. Only posts generated with Llama 3.3 scored, on average, higher on perceived humanness than human-authored posts. The social media platform also mattered, with participants distinguishing human from AI on most platforms (YouTube, TikTok, Truth Social), but not on X/Twitter. Incivility and negative emotions are associated with high humanness perceptions, and partisan identity also shaped evaluations, with Republican respondents more likely to view ideologically misaligned AI posts as AI-generated.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Humans show limited ability to distinguish human-authored from AI-generated political content on social media

abstract: Research has linked cultural differences to historical subsistence styles, but most studies have focused on farming or herding. Sea fishing is a major subsistence style, yet we know much less about whether fishing shapes culture. We propose an explanation for why fishing has received less attention—its cultural patterns do not fit neatly into the individualism-collectivism dichotomy that has been so useful in studies of farming and herding. First, we tested 1,010 people from nearby regions in Japan as a more controlled comparison. Then we tested the generalizability of the findings across 150 contemporary nations and historical records from 1,265 ethnic groups worldwide. People from fishing regions think holistically and emphasize responsibilities in close relationships more than people in nonfishing cultures (culture level d = 0.91). These characteristics are more common in collectivistic cultures and may have been adaptive for cooperation in dangerous seas. However, they show less ingroup loyalty and less outgroup discrimination (d = 1.37), which is more similar to individualistic cultures. Openness to outsiders may have been adaptive for fishing’s mobility and flexible labor networks. We address reverse causality by running instrumental variable analyses using data on environmental suitability for fishing. To pinpoint fishing, we compare regions that have coastlines, some by seas that support large fish populations and others that support few fish. Results show access to the ocean, trade, or transportation are not linked to these cultural differences. Finally, the cultural patterns do not extend to freshwater fishing, which has different demands from sea fishing.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Sea-fishing cultures show rare blend of tight social ties and openness to strangers

abstract: Undernutrition is the leading risk factor for tuberculosis susceptibility, severity, and poor treatment outcome. Nutritional immunology and immunometabolism frame how nutrient availability and metabolism shape host defense against Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) infection. By integrating targeted metabolomics and transcriptional profiling in a murine tuberculosis model, we defined immunometabolic programs underlying the transition from acute to chronic infection. Immune control of Mtb during acute infection was accompanied by robust activation of immune and metabolic programs, including mTORC1-associated signaling, glutaminolysis, glycolysis, arginine metabolism, and serine one-carbon metabolism, thereby highlighting the importance of amino acid metabolism and mitochondrial function in antimicrobial immunity. In contrast, chronic infection was characterized by reduced immune activation and mTORC1-associated signaling, increased branched-chain amino acid catabolism, and altered amino acid profiles, with leucine and glutamine among the discriminating metabolites. These findings suggest that reduced glutamine availability during chronic infection may increase reliance on leucine oxidative catabolism to sustain mitochondrial metabolism during nutrient stress, potentially limiting leucine availability for mTORC1-associated anabolic metabolism and immune activation. Oral glutamine supplementation restored amino acid homeostasis, including lung leucine abundance, enhanced mTORC1-associated signaling and central metabolic programs, moderately reduced bacterial burden and lung pathology, and mitigated infection-associated wasting. Reanalysis of published human metabolomics datasets further demonstrated reduced circulating glutamine levels during progression to active tuberculosis, supporting conservation of glutamine metabolic dysregulation across host species. Collectively, our findings identify a potential glutamine–leucine metabolic axis linking nutrient availability with immunometabolic competence and provide a mechanistic rationale for evaluating glutamine supplementation as a host-directed strategy for tuberculosis.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Immunometabolic basis of glutamine supplementation as a potential host-directed therapy for tuberculosis

abstract: The cocktail party problem—parsing relevant voices from competing speakers—has traditionally been studied as a sensory challenge for auditory cortex. Yet in natural communication, identifying speakers and coordinating interaction are inherently social processes. Here we recorded single neurons from anterior cingulate cortex (ACC, area 24) in freely moving marmosets engaged in spontaneous vocal exchanges within a noisy colony environment. ACC neurons selectively encoded vocalizations from a social partner versus other callers in the scene, effectively parsing speakers in the acoustic mixture. This selectivity was preserved even when vocalizations overlapped in time, indicating robustness to background interference. Apart from perception, ACC population activity represented vocal production, call type, and whether calls occurred within vocal turn-taking exchanges. Behaviorally, marmosets adjusted vocal timing based on the surrounding acoustic scene, and these interaction contexts were reliably reflected in ACC activity. Together, these findings suggest that neurons in ACC play a role in parsing conspecific speakers during communication in a natural “cocktail party,” linking auditory scene analysis with social monitoring and coordinated interactions.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Anterior cingulate cortex neurons parse speakers in a natural cocktail party

abstract: Parathyroid hormone receptor 1 (PTH1R) constitutively active mutants, including H223 2.50 R and T410 6.42 P, are responsible for Jansen’s metaphyseal chondrodysplasia, a form of short-limbed dwarfism. Here, we expand pharmacological understanding and present cryoelectron microscopy structures of the constitutively active PTH1R mutants, H223 2.50 K, H223 2.50 R, and T410 6.42 P, in complex with Gs protein and PTH(1–34), and H223 2.50 R and T410 6.42 P in the ligand free Gs complexed form. These reveal modifications in polar networks that allow for constitutive G protein coupling and subsequent signaling. In the absence of a peptide bound to the extracellular side of the PTH1R, TM6 adopts a distinct conformation relative to the PTH(1–34) bound wild-type PTH1R coupled with Gs. Combined with molecular dynamics analysis of inactive and Gs bound receptors, this work reveals distinct mechanisms that lead to differing receptor activation states and consequently promote distinct constitutive activity and agonist-mediated pharmacological profiles.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Structural and biochemical impact of clinically relevant constitutively active parathyroid hormone receptor 1 mutations

abstract: Birth–death models quantify macroevolutionary and epidemiological processes, including speciation, extinction, and transmission, based on phylogenetic trees. Extensions of these models incorporate external covariates as predictors of these parameters, for instance linking traits or environmental variables with changes in these rates. However, the dependencies between predictors and model parameters are typically restricted to linear, additive effects and may thus fail to capture complex, nonlinear relationships underlying evolutionary dynamics. To address this limitation, we propose a framework that leverages unsupervised Bayesian neural networks to flexibly model functional relationships between these parameters and a broad set of predictors, including categorical traits, quantitative variables, and time series data. Based on these covariates, the network weights and thus the resulting birth–death dynamics are estimated jointly with the phylogenetic tree, obtained directly from sequence alignment data. Extensive simulations show that this approach accurately recovers predictor–parameter relationships, mitigates overfitting, and remains robust across both macroevolutionary and epidemiological contexts. Using explainable AI, we further show that our framework reliably identifies the most influential predictors and yields interpretable descriptions of their impact on the inferred rates. Finally, we apply our method in two empirical analyses: linking SARS-CoV-2 migration dynamics with travel data during its early spread in Europe, and inferring trait- and time-dependent speciation and extinction rates in the diversification of platyrrhines. Our framework substantially expands the capabilities of birth–death models, providing a powerful and flexible approach to infer complex epidemiological and macroevolutionary processes.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Unsupervised Bayesian neural networks enable inference of complex epidemiological and macroevolutionary processes

abstract: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is an early and potentially reversible stage of neurodegenerative disease, yet its initiating pathogenic signal remains unclear. Here, we identify gut microbiota-derived, urease-dependent intestinal ammonia as an early functional contributor to cognitive impairment. Analyses of human MCI-related cohorts revealed increased fecal urease activity and ammonia-related microbial features associated with cognitive performance. Importantly, intestinal ammonia accumulation precedes detectable elevations in blood ammonia, indicating that local intestinal dysregulation occurs before systemic hyperammonemia. Mechanistically, ammonia suppresses colonic SMAD7 and activates JAK2 signaling in the brain, thereby promoting cognitive dysfunction independently of systemic ammonia toxicity. This signaling pattern was further supported in 5xFAD mice. Therapeutically, supplementation with the ammonia-assimilating bacterium Limosilactobacillus mucosae or treatment with the clinically used ammonia-lowering agent L-ornithine-L-aspartate reduces intestinal ammonia levels and ameliorates early cognitive deficits. Together, these findings define an ammonia-SMAD7-JAK2 axis linking gut metabolism to brain function and highlight intestinal ammonia as a promising therapeutic target for early cognitive impairment.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Beyond blood ammonia: Intestinal ammonia emerges as an early microbial driver of mild cognitive impairment

abstract: Infection with the gammaherpesvirus Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) is the strongest environmental risk factor for multiple sclerosis (MS). This risk is driven by poor immune control of viral replication, which is genetically determined. Clonally expanded CD8 T cells are abundant in MS lesions, and some recognize EBV antigens. We previously demonstrated that host genetic variation regulates immune control of the homologous B cell-tropic murine gammaherpesvirus, MHV-68. Here, we investigated how gammaherpesvirus infection and host genotype shape central nervous system (CNS) T cell responses, before and after induction of experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE). Chronic infection alone was sufficient to promote a marked accumulation of CX3CR1+KLRG1+ effector CD8 T cells and CX3CR1+KLRG1+ cytotoxic-like T helper cells in the CNS of MHV-68-susceptible C57BL/6 mice. T cells localized to brain border regions and throughout the CNS parenchyma. MHC tetramer analysis demonstrated that CNS-infiltrating T cells were specific for viral antigens, and viral DNA was detectable in CNS-infiltrating leukocytes during early and chronic infection. EAE further amplified cytotoxic T cell accumulation in the CNS of MHV-68-infected C57BL/6 mice. However, CNS T cell infiltration was highly attenuated in genetically divergent wild-derived PWD/PhJ mice, which control MHV-68 more effectively, but not in MHV-68-susceptible 129S1/SvImJ mice. Surprisingly, chronic MHV-68 infection modestly delayed EAE onset in C57BL/6 mice, an effect reversed by B cell depletion. Together with emerging human studies, our results suggest that host genetic variation contributes to poor control of EBV in MS, promoting virus-specific cytotoxic T cell accumulation in the CNS and immune reprogramming both before and during autoimmune neuroinflammation.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Gammaherpesvirus infection drives genotype-dependent virus-specific T cell responses in the CNS prior to autoimmune neuroinflammation

abstract: Photolysis of nitrous acid (HONO) drives ozone and secondary aerosol formation, yet its sources remain poorly constrained. We identify HONO emissions from decaying aboveground plant residues as a previously overlooked plant-derived component of terrestrial HONO emissions. Field observations and dual-isotope (15 N– 18 O) tracing reveal that HONO arises mainly from nitrate reduction within decomposing plants. We integrated global datasets on vegetation nitrate, litter decomposition, soil, and climate to estimate HONO emissions from vegetation decay at 1.1 ± 0.1 Tg N y −1. This substantially narrows the long-standing uncertainty in HONO budget. This plant-mediated pathway extends the soil-atmosphere paradigm to soil-plant-atmosphere framework. Moreover, we identify emission hotspots and drivers, assess their climate-driven shifts, and propose region-specific mitigation strategies. These findings uncover a missing link between terrestrial nitrogen cycling and atmospheric reactivity, highlighting biogeochemical controls on air quality.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Vegetation decay enhances terrestrial nitrous acid emissions through nitrate reduction

abstract: Biomolecular condensates control the spatial and temporal organization of cellular biochemistry. Their architectures often arise from complex, multicomponent mixtures governed by weak, multivalent interactions between intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs) of proteins. However, current approaches lack generalizable metrics to determine whether IDRs will mix or segregate within condensates. Here, we present a domain decomposition method (DDM) that accurately determines phase concentrations without identifying condensate interfaces. When tested against 399 IDR simulations, the DDM recovers dense- and dilute-phase concentrations within 1% agreement of established surface-based methods. By calculating spatial variances to map three-dimensional organization, this approach successfully distinguishes homogeneous mixing from surface enrichment, core–shell architectures, and complete segregation. Applying this continuous metric to 2,068 binary mixtures of 32 distinct IDRs, we demonstrate that physicochemical similarity strongly promotes mixing. Hydrophobic IDRs mixed promiscuously across all partner chemistries, whereas charged sequences mixed in a way highly sensitive to charge complementarity, forming the most stable condensates as net charge approached zero. Compared with experimental networks, our IDR-only simulations predicted the partitioning preferences for 10 of 13 proteins, with discrepancies accurately isolating cases where colocalization strictly requires RNA or folded domains. Quantifying mixing in this way provides a robust and reproducible method for predicting IDR interactomes and understanding the composition of complex cellular condensates.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Quantifying (de)mixing of disordered proteins in molecular dynamics simulations

abstract: High-nickel cathodes provide high capacity in lithium-ion batteries; however, their slow lithiation reactions require a prolonged high-temperature hold during synthesis which is directly responsible for high manufacturing cost. Here, we report that the precursor morphology and crystallinity can be engineered to regulate the nucleation and growth of the layered phase at temperatures as low as 575 °C. We use nanosheets of NiO and Ni(OH) 2 with high specific surface areas to maximize the contact area between Li and Ni precursors and to shorten Li + diffusion lengths. Highly crystalline NiO seeds early and uniform layered phase nucleation at low temperatures. Preheating Ni(OH) 2 to NiO at 300 °C maintains the large surface area and yields a higher layered fraction with limited lamellae coarsening. Preheating at 500 °C produces more crystalline NiO seeds that promote the synchronous Ni oxidation and cation ordering upon layered phase formation to deliver higher discharge capacity and better rate capability than conventionally synthesized LiNiO 2. In contrast, along the hydroxide-based route, in situ generated Li 2 CO 3 disrupts wetting and hampers lithiation, ultimately trapping lithium within a disordered rocksalt intermediate. This work demonstrates that precursor morphology, crystallinity, and processing temperature control lithiation kinetics, providing broad guidance for energy-efficient synthesizing advanced oxide battery cathodes.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Precursor-engineered lithiation kinetics enable low-temperature synthesis of Li–Ni–O positive electrode materials

abstract: Patient movement within and between hospitals creates a complex hospital network that facilitates the spread of antimicrobial-resistant bacteria and contributes to healthcare-associated infections. Yet most national-scale studies infer spread from aggregated hospital-to-hospital patient sharing, leaving patient-to-patient contact pathways and the role of routine patient mobility in shaping colonization risk poorly characterized. Using France’s 2023–2024 national hospital-discharge data, we reconstructed a temporal patient-based network of 10.4 million patients across 1,408 acute-care hospitals, comprising 326.6 million overnight ward colocation interactions. We simulated colonization over 365 d on the observed day-by-day temporal network using a stochastic susceptible–colonized–susceptible model, with a mean colonization duration of 180 d. We used national carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales (CPE) surveillance data to calibrate differences in transmission risk across clinical settings. Across 2,000 simulations initiated on randomly selected dates in 2023, we calculated patient-level colonization probabilities and summarized risk across patients’ residential areas, wards, and hospitals. We further assessed hospital-level consistency between simulated risk and recorded CPE occurrence. Simulated risk was highly heterogeneous across patients and care settings. When mapped by place of residence, hospital-associated colonization risk showed strong spatial clustering in both urban and rural areas. Multivariable regression analyses identified patient- and hospital-level characteristics associated with heterogeneity in simulated colonization risk. Sensitivity analyses varying initial seeding and colonization duration showed that relative risk patterns remained highly stable. This nationwide framework shows how patient mobility and ward colocation patterns can reveal patterns of hospital-associated colonization risk and could support pathogen-specific surveillance and intervention evaluation.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Evidence for patterns of colonization risk in the nationwide hospitalized patient network in France

abstract: Societies rely on groups–boards, panels, committees, and representative bodies–to make important decisions for good reason: overwhelming evidence shows groups usually make more accurate choices than individuals. The predominant logic for group accuracy rests on reasoning formulated in the Condorcet Jury Theorem, which states that if voters receive independent and equally accurate generated signals, majority rule produces decisions that i) are more accurate than the average voter, ii) improve in individual accuracy and iii) group size, and iv) approach perfect accuracy as group size becomes large. An alternative logic based on interpreted signals explains the accuracy of majority rule as arising from the aggregation of diverse mental models. Group accuracy results from the same state of the world being classified differently by different people. In this framework, the set of possible group accuracies can be characterized conditional on average individual accuracy and average pairwise diversity. Majority rule groups are only guaranteed to outperform their members when diversity is high. Using data from a variety of empirical settings, along with simulations of a minimal nearest-neighbor model, we find much stronger support for the predictions of the interpreted signals framework than for the standard generated signals model. We further show empirical evidence for a diversity–accuracy paradox, in which more diverse groups are less accurate unless average individual accuracy is nearly constant across groups. Our findings have important implications for group composition and institutional and organizational design as well as for the potential gains from deliberation.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Cognitive diversity and majority rule

abstract: The cell theory of aging posits that senescent cells accumulate with age, altering their environment and causing functional organ decline. The dynamics of their accumulation during normal aging and the extent to which it contributes to age-associated damage and disease remain unclear. Using the Study of Longitudinal Aging in Mice, which tracks two strains in both sexes, we identified skin health as a strong predictor of frailty. Quantification of three canonical senescence-associated markers (p16, p21, and γH2AX) in the skin of 320 animals showed variable effects of age on marker abundance: p16 increased with age, whereas p21 and γH2AX showed little or nonuniform changes. Associations between marker burden and age-related phenotypes were highly heterogeneous and varied by marker, sex, and strain. These findings underscore a complex, context-dependent relationship between senescence-associated markers and aging phenotypes, challenging the view that senescent cell accumulation uniformly drives organ decline.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Senescence markers diverge in space, timing, and phenotypic relevance during skin aging in mice

abstract: The effect of noninertial dynamics on static quantum resource theories is investigated. To this end, we first show the equivalence between noninertial effects and a completely positive, trace-preserving (CPTP) map. In this formulation, the Unruh effect is equivalent to a bosonic amplifier channel. The effect of this map on a generic quantum resource is investigated by studying the role of the CPTP map on the three core ingredients of a resource theory, namely, the free states, the free operations, and the resource quantifiers. We show several general statements can be made about these three components of a resource theory in the presence of noninertial motion.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Influence of noninertial dynamics on static quantum resource theories

abstract: The polar plateaus are among the most remote environments on Earth. Despite their extreme conditions, these cold deserts on the Greenland and Antarctic Ice Sheets harbor microbial life in snow, ice, and air. However, knowledge of polar airborne microbiomes remains scarce and methodological differences have hindered bipolar comparisons. Here, we present a systematic survey of airborne bacterial and eukaryotic communities across Greenlandic and Antarctic Plateaus, using standardized sampling and genetic techniques, coupled with atmospheric physics and advanced statistical analyses. We found that Antarctic airborne communities are characterized by low diversity and high homogeneity, whereas Greenlandic communities are richer, more variable, and more connected to coastal-marine zones. Our results indicate that atmospheric isolation, together with short-term atmospheric variables, is associated with differences in the microbial biogeography of each Plateau. Compared with Antarctica, the Greenlandic Plateau is more frequently influenced by air masses from outside the plateau over long timescales and exhibits more variable short-term air back-trajectories, reflecting enhanced microbial dispersal and diversity. These findings highlight the potential of polar plateaus as observational platforms for airborne microbial diversity, where sustained and temporally resolved sampling could help assess variations in community composition associated with atmospheric circulation and anthropogenic influence under global change.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Airborne microbial diversity over Greenlandic and Antarctic plateaus reflects divergent atmospheric connectivity

abstract: The human retina is perfused by capillary plexuses at distinct inner-retinal depths. Interconnections among these plexuses are critical for perfusion, but are difficult to quantify using 2D en face optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA). Diabetic retinopathy (DR) involves extensive microvascular remodeling, however the topological changes, especially at the interplexus level, are challenging to assess in vivo. We introduce Network Analysis using Vascular Interconnectivity (NAVI) OCTA, a framework that reconstructs the 3D retinal capillary network across the superficial vascular (SVP), intermediate capillary (ICP), and deep capillary (DCP) plexuses. The reconstructed macula-wide vasculature contains more than 10,000 vessel segments, and can be quantitatively analyzed using network representation. This method reveals a divergent alteration in interplexus connectivity in early DR: superficial-to-intermediate connections decrease, while intermediate-to-deep connections increase. This finding is consistent with previous histological studies, but is quantitatively measured in vivo in the human retina, opening the possibility for longitudinal studies of capillary remodeling. In addition to size-based metrics (e.g., vessel length or area), NAVI can quantify recurrent small-scale connectivity patterns (motifs). Finally, joint connectivity-hemodynamics analysis is demonstrated in eyes with DR, where capillary topology and flow speed can be quantified using a single OCTA acquisition. NAVI OCTA is a scalable, computational framework that supports analysis of retinal vasculature as a network and provides an in vivo approach to study capillary remodeling in early DR.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Human retinal capillary network analysis using vascular interconnectivity optical coherence tomography angiography

abstract: Protein complexes are essential for cellular functions, with their dynamics increasingly recognized as key regulatory elements. In the cyanobacterial circadian clock, the KaiC hexamer is highly dynamic, undergoing phosphorylation-dependent monomer shuffling that synchronizes individual oscillators. However, the molecular mechanism of monomer shuffling is not fully understood. Here we combine a chromatography-based method with single-molecule fluorescence microscopy to quantify subunit exchange in the hexamerization domain of KaiC (KaiC-CI) and in full-length KaiC. We show that ATPase activity is essential for monomer shuffling. Through quantitative modeling of experimental data, we found that adenosine triphosphate (ATP) hydrolysis at two independent monomer–monomer interfaces disassembles a KaiC-CI hexamer into two oligomers. Two complementary oligomers from two different hexamers can rapidly reform a mixed hexamer. Mechanistically, ATP hydrolysis induces unstable, shuffling-competent states in hexamers, while nucleotide exchange stabilizes them, suppressing shuffling. The balance between these two processes quantitatively explains the relationship between shuffling rate and ATPase activity across KaiC mutants observed in our experiments. Applying this model to full-length KaiC revealed that phosphorylation of the KaiC-CII domain modulates shuffling primarily by affecting the nucleotide exchange rate in the CI domain. This establishes a feedback loop where CII phosphorylation alters CI ATPase activity, which in turn controls subunit exchange to synchronize CII phosphorylation across the KaiC hexamer population. Our findings provide a mechanistic framework linking ATPase-driven subunit exchange to the robustness of circadian clocks, with implications for activation-coupled dynamics in other molecular machines.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Phosphorylation-dependent ATPase activity regulates subunit shuffling dynamics in cyanobacterial circadian clock proteins

abstract: Meiotic recombination reshuffles genetic diversity through reciprocal DNA exchanges between chromosomes known as crossovers. In most eukaryotes, crossovers are highly constrained in both frequency and distribution, leaving large genomic regions with little or no recombination. A notable exception is the Brassica AAC allotriploid hybrid obtained from a cross between allotetraploid Brassica napus (AACC) and diploid Brassica rapa (AA), which exhibits elevated recombination and crossover formation near centromeres. Here, we generated a CCA allotriploid hybrid from a cross between B. napus and Brassica oleracea (CC), and subsequently produced AAC allotriploids by crossing the CCA hybrid with B. rapa. Both CCA and AAC allotriploids exhibit similar meiotic deregulation, demonstrating that this phenomenon is not restricted to AAC hybrids. Both systems displayed a marked increase in crossover frequency within normally low-recombining chromosome regions, reaching 9.4-fold in AAC and 13.4-fold in CCA allotriploids. Alternating CCA and AAC allotriploids efficiently reshuffled both B. napus subgenomes within only two generations. Using genetic mapping and cytogenetics, we further identified homoeologous exchanges. Remarkably, crossovers occurring on chromosomes involved in homoeologous associations exhibited a more pronounced redistribution toward nonrecombining regions than those on homologously paired chromosomes. Moreover, the frequency of homoeologous associations varied with the diploid progenitor genotype, indicating that genetic factors controlling homoeologous recombination already exist in Brassica diploids. Altogether, our results identify allotriploidy as a simple and powerful strategy to unlock recombination deserts, which harbor 21% of total resistance gene analogs, and provide insights into its potential role in allopolyploid evolution, adaptation, and speciation.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Interploidy massively increases meiotic crossovers in pericentromeric recombination deserts

abstract: Plants have evolved sophisticated defense strategies against herbivory, often releasing volatile compounds upon attack to deter further feeding. Here, we demonstrate the induced volatile S-linalool promotes phase- and stage-specific group foraging in the migratory locust (Locusta migratoria). We show that S-linalool, a volatile whose emission increases more than 10-fold following damage by gregarious nymphs, acts as a potent attractant that drives other nymphs to aggregate and feed on previously attacked rice plants. Mechanistically, we identified the olfactory receptor LmOR49 that detects S-linalool and used genome editing to make this receptor nonfunctional, thereby abolishing both electrophysiological responses and behavioral attraction. We also inactivated rice genes required for S-linalool biosynthesis, abolishing its emission, rendering plants unattractive, and disrupting locust feeding preference. Although feeding on previously attacked plants provides no detectable direct fitness benefit under our experimental conditions, prior locust feeding suppresses the accumulation of deterrent metabolites, potentially increasing plant palatability for subsequent feeding. S-linalool thus serves as an olfactory cue that guides gregarious nymphs toward previously attacked, more palatable plants. Collectively, these findings uncover a comprehensive mechanism whereby a plant defense volatile is exploited by an insect herbivore to promote group foraging, broadening our understanding of plant–insect interactions and suggesting molecular targets for locust control.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: A herbivore-induced plant volatile facilitates group foraging in locusts

abstract: Wingless/Int-1 (Wnts) are secreted glycoproteins and canonical Frizzled receptor ligands. Recent evidence indicates that some Wnts can also bind to polycystin 1 (PKD1), a large transmembrane protein which can couple to polycystin 2 (PKD2) to form a nonselective cation channel. The functional significance of PKD1, PKD2, and Wnt-mediated PKD1 signaling in native cell types is poorly understood. Here, we tested the hypothesis that Wnts regulate arterial contractility, investigated the signaling mechanisms and cell types involved, and examined the cellular source of vasoactive Wnts. Our data show that Wnt9b and Wnt5a are endothelial cell (EC)-dependent vasodilators. Wnt9b stimulates vasodilation via EC PKD1/PKD2, whereas Wnt5a acts via both EC PKD1/PKD2 and Frizzled receptors. Wnts stimulate endothelial nitric oxide synthase and small conductance Ca 2+ -activated K + channels in ECs to produce vasodilation. Wnt9b and Wnt5a are present in plasma and intravenous infusion of Wnt9b stimulates an EC PKD1-dependent reduction in systemic blood pressure. Intravascular flow activates angiotensin II type 1 receptors which, through G q/11 and Porcupine signaling, stimulate ECs to secrete Wnt9b and Wnt5a. Wnts which are secreted by ECs in response to flow activate PKD1/PKD2 on ECs and this mechanism contributes to the flow-mediated vasodilation. In summary, we show that Wnts are autocrine/paracrine vasodilator proteins. Intravascular flow stimulates ECs to secrete Wnts, which then act via PKD1/PKD2 and Frizzled receptors on ECs to induce vasodilation.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Wnts are endothelial cell–derived PKD1/PKD2-dependent autocrine/paracrine vasodilators

abstract: Cadmium contamination of staple cereals is an important food-safety concern, yet how long-term changes in soil chemistry alter cadmium transfer into food remains poorly resolved. Here we reconstructed changes in cropland topsoil cadmium and pH across China from 1980 to 2020 and quantified their consequences for cereal grain cadmium, dietary exposure, and mitigation potential. National mean topsoil cadmium increased from 0.123 to 0.236 mg kg −1, while mean cropland pH declined from 6.50 to 6.30 nationally and by about 0.5 units in several southern rice-growing provinces. These coupled changes increased mean grain cadmium from 0.043 to 0.100 mg kg −1 in rice and from 0.017 to 0.032 mg kg −1 in wheat. By 2020, provinces with estimated mean hazard quotients exceeded 1.0 had a combined population of about 138 million. Counterfactual analysis showed that soil cadmium accumulation remained the dominant driver of rising grain cadmium, while acidification substantially amplified soil-to-grain transfer, especially in rice systems. Scenario analysis to 2050 indicated that restoring cropland pH to 6.5 could offset about 44% of the projected increase in rice cadmium even without immediate source control, whereas combining pH restoration with source control reduced mean rice cadmium by about 59% and brought exceedance close to zero. These findings identify soil acidification as an important amplifier of cadmium transfer into staple cereals and highlight targeted cropland pH restoration as a practical near-term strategy for reducing food-chain exposure while longer-term source-control measures take effect.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Soil contamination and acidification jointly increased cereal cadmium and dietary exposure over four decades

abstract: Darwinian neurodynamics posits that the brain searches large solution spaces through iterated cycles of variation and selection on competing neural representations. Testing this hypothesis requires a biologically plausible neural replicator: a mechanism that copies spatiotemporal signals faithfully enough to cumulatively improve good solutions, yet loosely enough to allow exploration. We show that phase-coded spike patterns constitute such a replicator. Spike timing referenced to a local field oscillation is compressed into a transferable spike train and reconstructed by coincidence with the receiver's own field, without synaptic plasticity or a shared code key. As replication noise rises, the system crosses two thresholds. Below the first, faithful copying sustains patterns as dynamic memory. Between the two thresholds, pattern populations evolve. On two hard combinatorial benchmarks, the traveling salesman problem and NK fitness landscapes, neural replication remains competitive with standard search methods at a matched evaluation budget. Beyond the second, an Eigen-like error threshold, inherited information collapses. The network architecture tunes the exploration-exploitation balance: high-degree lattices, where local competition is stronger, exploit smooth landscapes, while low-degree lattices, where weaker competition preserves diversity, search more broadly on rugged landscapes. The framework predicts phase-locked information transfer and phylogenetic structure in replay, as well as a selective loss of combinatorial problem solving beyond the error threshold. These results indicate that a single neurobiological substrate can support memory, variation, and selection, and point to evolutionary dynamics as a candidate computational principle for cognition.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Phase coding supports neuronal replication and enables combinatorial problem solving

abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is characterized by pathogenic humoral autoimmunity, yet the mechanisms linking T cell dysfunction to aberrant B cell responses remain poorly defined. Here, we identify a CD8 + T cell–intrinsic metabolic defect that promotes humoral immune dysregulation in lupus. CD8 + T cells from patients with SLE exhibited elevated CD38 expression associated with reduced intracellular NAD + levels, mitochondrial dysfunction, and impaired cytotoxic capacity. Pharmacologic inhibition of CD38 with the small-molecule inhibitor MK-0159 restored NAD + metabolism and rescued cytotoxic function in human CD8 + T cells ex vivo. To selectively target this pathway in vivo, we developed anti-CD8 antibody-conjugated nanoparticles encapsulating MK-0159. In lupus-prone MRL/ lpr mice, CD8-targeted delivery enhanced granzyme B expression, improved degranulation, reduced plasmablast responses and autoantibody production, immune complex deposition, and renal pathology. Importantly, targeted delivery restored CD8 + T cell function without broad immune perturbation. These findings identify CD38-driven NAD + depletion as a reversible immunometabolic checkpoint limiting CD8 + T cell cytotoxic competence and support a model in which targeted restoration of cytotoxic fitness contributes to the control of humoral autoimmunity in SLE.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Targeted metabolic reprogramming of CD8 T cells restores immune regulation in lupus

abstract: Neuropathic pain involves persistent metabolic and transcriptional remodeling in spinal microglia, but the mechanisms linking these processes remain unclear. Time-resolved single-cell RNA sequencing after chronic constriction injury identified increased PRMT5 expression in glycolysis-enriched activated microglia. Microglia-specific Prmt5 deletion or pharmacological inhibition reduced glycolytic remodeling and pain hypersensitivity. Mechanistically, PRMT5 associated with alanyl-tRNA synthetase 1 (AARS1), promoted AARS1-associated symmetric dimethylation and nuclear accumulation, and supported AARS1-dependent H3K18la and H4K12la. Disrupting AARS1 nuclear localization impaired histone lactylation and glycolytic responses. The pathway was validated in primary microglia, spinal microglia, and female mice. Chromatin profiling linked injury-associated histone lactylation to glycolytic gene programs. Finally, biomimetic siPRMT5 nanoparticles preferentially reduced PRMT5 in spinal microglia and alleviated pain hypersensitivity. These findings identify a PRMT5–AARS1–histone lactylation pathway that reinforces microglial glycolytic reprogramming and represents a potential therapeutic target for neuropathic pain.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: PRMT5 licenses AARS1-dependent histone lactylation to amplify microglial glycolytic reprogramming in neuropathic pain

abstract: Biological tissues must dynamically transition between solid-like and fluid-like states during processes like morphogenesis and collective migration, often while resisting physiological shear stresses. It remains unclear whether these transitions in tissue dynamics are governed by the same nonequilibrium critical phenomena that control conventional disordered matter. Here we show that the flow response of model cell monolayers under constant shear stress is described by universal scaling behavior, with different flow regimes controlled by the same underlying physical parameters. This framework captures regimes in which the underlying system has both rigid and fluid-like behavior in the absence of imposed fluctuations and stresses. In the rigid regime, small internal fluctuations maintain a solid-like state up to a finite yield stress before the tissue shear thins; the fluid-like regime instead exhibits robust continuous and discontinuous shear thickening. We demonstrate that at high enough stress, the fluid-like regime undergoes structural arrest. This space-filling shear-jamming transition is accompanied by structural changes, including the formation of system-spanning force chains and the emergence of orientational ordering. These results establish confluent tissues as a distinct class of disordered matter, demonstrating that complex nonlinear rheology and structural arrest can emerge entirely through shape-driven topological constraints to regulate biological mechanics.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Universal scaling in the rheology of dense cellular systems

abstract: The prey choice model, widely applied in archaeological reconstructions of Pleistocene diet, predicts that people will initially focus on a narrow suite of high-ranked prey before broadening their diet to include lower-ranked species as necessitated by subsistence needs. However, evidence from arid and semiarid northern Australia challenges this assumption. Archaeological faunal records demonstrate that a broad diet was established early and persisted through the Holocene. We argue that these diverse diets do not indicate resource scarcity, but rather represent an ideal strategy for exploiting abundant, low-risk hidden, or cryptic prey, as well as high-risk, conspicuous prey within an environment characterized by unpredictable rainfall. This pattern also necessitates reconceptualizing traditional notions of prey rank and dietary breadth. Rather than adhering to static prey rankings, northern Australian peoples skillfully adapted their hunting strategies in response to fluctuating nutritional content and pursuit costs of different species. The most successful subsistence strategy in this region was therefore one of high responsiveness and flexibility, manifesting as a consistently broad diet. This case study suggests that the relationship between human dietary breadth and resource abundance is more nuanced in situations of abundant, cryptic prey.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Rethinking broad diet breadth as a sign of scarcity: A 50,000-y record of subsistence from northwestern Australia

abstract: Soft composites are increasingly used in wearable and soft robotic systems, as advances in material architecture enable greater damage tolerance under large deformation. In these mesoscale architectures, the crack-parallel stresses modify the crack initiation and growth in the opening-mode fracture. Emulating the gap test, we introduce a fracture test to quantify how the superposed crack-parallel tension affects the maximum load (i.e., the load capacity) and the load-deflection curve. A Mode I (opening mode) center-notched tensioned strip is used because its advantages in generating crack-parallel tension outweigh its hypothetical disadvantages with possible instability of crack jumps at two competing crack fronts. We develop and experimentally validate a continuum model that captures the nonlinear behavior and progressive damage of knitted composites. To this end, we introduce an ensemble of oriented microplane triads tangential to the yarn at characteristic points of the yarn loop within a repetitive unit cell of the knit. The triads ensure the yarn-polymer transfer of all normal and shear stress components at each characteristic point. The experimentally calibrated computational model provides a tool to predict the effect of crack-parallel tension on the changes of load capacity and of the effective fracture energy of knitted polymer composites, enabling rational design of these composites in engineering applications such as wearables and soft robotics.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Gap test–inspired crack-parallel tension tests of fracture of soft-knitted polymer composites simulated by microplane triads

abstract: Rotavirus replication, pathogenesis, and transmission are host-range restricted, yet the viral and host determinants remain poorly defined. Rotavirus nonstructural protein 1 (NSP1) is a multifunctional innate immune antagonist dispensable for replication in permissive cells. Here, using reverse genetics, neonatal mice, intestinal organoids, and comparative proteomics, we identify mouse SAMD9L as a critical host restriction factor selectively antagonized by murine rotavirus-encoded NSP1. An NSP1-deletion murine-like rotavirus produced progeny efficiently in cell lines but was highly attenuated in neonatal mice with no productive intestinal replication, fecal shedding, and diarrhea. Recombinant monoreassortant viruses carrying NSP1 genes from rhesus, bovine, or human rotavirus strains did not support murine intestinal infection, even in Stat1 −/− pups, indicating an additional restriction mechanism beyond STAT1-dependent antiviral signaling. Comparative proteomics identified mouse SAMD9L as a specific interactor of murine NSP1, and NSP1 promoted SAMD9L degradation through a neddylation- and proteasome-dependent pathway. AlphaFold3 guided mutagenesis identified NSP1 residues S364/E366 and SAMD9L residues R455/L462 as functionally important for the NSP1–SAMD9L interaction. Mutations on either side disrupted NSP1–SAMD9L association and prevented SAMD9L degradation. Replication of murine rotaviruses carrying S364A or E366A mutations was undetectable in wild-type mice and was restored in Samd9l −/− mice. Combined deletion of Samd9l and Stat1 permitted replication of otherwise attenuated viruses carrying mismatched NSP1s and enabled fecal IgA seroconversion after a single oral inoculation of Rotarix. These findings identify SAMD9L as a physiologically relevant intestinal restriction factor in mice and show that murine NSP1 antagonism of mouse SAMD9L contributes to murine rotavirus host range restriction in vivo.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: NSP1–SAMD9L interactions govern murine rotavirus host range restriction in vivo

abstract: Biomolecular structure prediction tools such as AlphaFold have achieved remarkable success in predicting structures of single proteins and multiprotein complexes. AlphaFold3 now incorporates the capability to model complexes containing nucleic acids and chemically modified side chains. Investigators can now predict structures of proteins bound to chromatin, where interactions with nucleosomal DNA and histone posttranslational modifications (PTMs) converge to control genome function. To evaluate its robustness in modeling chromatin complexes, we benchmarked AlphaFold3 on 115 structures containing nucleosomes whose coordinates were released by the Protein Data Bank after the training set cutoff date. We find that AlphaFold3 excels at predicting interactions with the histone octamer core and with PTMs. By contrast, AlphaFold3 struggles to predict structures of chromatin factors that primarily engage nucleosomal DNA, notably transcription factors and chromatin remodelers. We also show that AlphaFold3 can faithfully recapitulate known PTM recognition patterns, matching experimentally determined specificity profiles. This assessment of the capabilities and limitations of AlphaFold3 in chromatin structural biology provides a roadmap for its effective application to studies of chromatin regulation and PTM readout, while identifying key areas for future refinement of algorithms for predicting interactions between proteins and nucleic acids.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: A chromatin biology assessment of AlphaFold3

abstract: Marine protists are key players in marine ecosystems, yet a large fraction, particularly among the smallest taxa, belongs to uncultured lineages lacking genomic data, limiting our understanding of their ecology and evolution. Beyond determining their gene repertoires, genomic information is essential to reveal how genomes are organized. Features such as genome size, GC content, and structural gene architecture represent physical constraints that shape evolutionary fitness and adaptability in marine environments. Here, we present a genomic catalog of 147 marine picoplanktonic protist species, greatly expanding the genomic representation of uncultured and ecologically relevant lineages through a single-cell approach. This dataset enables refined phylogenomic placement of previously uncharacterized marine eukaryotes, including abundant marine protistan players as well as a few species belonging to novel or poorly known groups that are crucial for resolving deep questions in eukaryotic evolution. We uncover pronounced genome streamlining in ecologically successful lineages, coupled with extensive, mostly lineage-specific functional adaptations. At a broader scale, we identify functional traits enriched independently across several marine eukaryotic lineages, including genes involved in complex carbohydrate degradation in heterotrophic organisms and the presence of polyketide synthases. Together, these results provide a framework for investigating the genomic drivers and molecular mechanisms behind the ecological success of marine eukaryotic microbes.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Single-cell genomics reveals genome streamlining and functional traits in dominant uncultured marine protists

abstract: Leishmaniasis affects approximately 1 million people annually with visceral infections resulting in death if left untreated and the cutaneous disease leading to disfiguring skin lesions. Leishmaniasis is caused by the Leishmania spp. parasites and is difficult to treat as existing drugs are far from optimal. Despite increased efforts to identify better drugs for leishmaniasis, there are few new chemical entities that have entered clinical development, thus highlighting the persistent need for such compounds. Here we describe GNF5885, an orally available and parasite-selective inhibitor of Leishmania cytochrome bc1 complex. GNF5885 was derived through phenotypic optimization of buparvaquone. GNF5885 exhibits unparalleled efficacy in vivo and can efficiently clear parasites from mice in models of visceral and cutaneous infections. Furthermore, its ability to clear parasites rapidly with short treatment regimens makes it particularly desirable for treating patients residing in regions endemic to leishmaniasis. Cryo-EM structure of the Leishmania cytochrome bc1 complex with GNF5885 at 2.8 Å resolution revealed that the inhibitor binds in the Qi ubiquinone-binding pocket. Our data provide validation of the Leishmania cytochrome bc1 complex as a promising therapeutic target for the treatment of leishmaniasis and underscore the possibility of developing a short-course oral treatment for this neglected disease. In addition, the availability of the cytochrome bc1 complex costructure with GNF5885 opens an opportunity to rationally design new cytochrome bc1 complex inhibitors suitable for clinical development.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Leishmania cytochrome bc1 complex inhibition has potential for shortening leishmaniasis treatment duration

abstract: The transcription factor E47, encoded by the TCF3 gene, is essential for B and T cell lineage commitment and development. However, whether tumor cell–intrinsic E47 contributes to tumor immunosurveillance remains unknown. In this study, we demonstrate that E47 functions as a critical suppressor of antitumor immunity. Clinical analyses reveal that increased intratumoral TCF3 expression is associated with an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Silencing of E47 in tumor cells markedly inhibits tumor growth, increases infiltration of cytotoxic CD8 + T cells, and decreases PD-L1 expression. Mechanistically, E47 transcriptionally represses FBXL2, which encodes an E3 ubiquitin ligase that promotes PD-L1 polyubiquitination at K270 and proteasomal degradation. Restoration of FBXL2 effectively reverses E47-induced PD-L1 upregulation and tumor growth. Strikingly, Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved drug nebivolol, an activator of FBXL2, significantly enhances antitumor immunity and improves the efficacy of CTLA-4 blockade therapy in syngeneic tumor mouse models. Together, this study uncovers the E47–FBXL2 axis as a critical pathway governing PD-L1 stability and antitumor immunity, highlighting its therapeutic potential for improving the efficacy of cancer immunotherapy.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Tumor cell–intrinsic E47 functions as a critical suppressor in antitumor immunity via the FBXL2–PD-L1 axis

abstract: Synthetic data have become an indispensable tool for validation, standards development, and product design across a broad range of scientific and engineering disciplines. One of the earliest examples arose in energy systems, where security and confidentiality constraints motivated the development of synthetic power grids and, in turn, novel topological and geometric approaches for evaluating their fidelity. Today, synthetic scientific imagery has emerged as a new critical tool in a variety of applications, ranging from autonomous driving, robotics, and Internet-of-Things technologies to in silico trials, digital twins, and remote sensing of environment. Yet the rigorous assessment of such synthetic images and quantification of their associated uncertainties remains a fundamental challenge. Building on the recent advances in the topological and geometric validation of synthetic power grids, we develop a systematic framework for comparing image data through the persistence of their multiscale shape patterns using the statistical formalism of survival analysis. While the tools of persistent homology and statistical survival analysis are both mature methodologies, they have so far developed largely in isolation. Unlike more traditional comparison methods such as pixel-level similarity or distributional summaries that often fail to capture the complex, multiscale structural characteristics of modern scientific imagery, our approach shows the capability to systematically assess the mismatch between different images at all scales simultaneously, while characterizing the associated uncertainty. The resulting synergistic methodology establishes a broadly applicable statistical topological framework for validating synthetic scientific imagery and, more generally, complex synthetic data products.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Topological validation of generated scientific images

abstract: We present a theoretical analysis of an induced seismic rupture propagating from a gas reservoir into the underburden. We use linear elastic fracture mechanics to determine the conditions for self-arrested or runaway ruptures. We derive a phase diagram in which the model parameters (the reservoir thickness, the reservoir pressure depletion, background stress, and fracture energy) are combined into two dimensionless parameters. We apply the analysis to the seismicity induced by gas extraction from the Groningen gas field, where earthquakes have remained confined to the close vicinity of the reservoir. We invert the observations for the model parameters. They indicate subcritical initial stress on the underburden faults, meaning that runaway ruptures are possible in principle, but the conditions required for such events to have happened were most likely not met in reality. The model reproduces the spatial and temporal patterns of observed maximum earthquake magnitudes, and the significant deficit of M > 3.0 events compared to the expectation from the Gutenberg–Richter relationship. This tapering implies that the expected maximum magnitude is nearly insensitive to the total number of induced earthquakes and strongly controlled by the reservoir thickness and pressure depletion. Because the forecast is probabilistic and accounts for uncertainties in the model parameters, it does not exclude runaway ruptures; but such events are found to be unlikely. The model offers an operational framework to forecast earthquake magnitudes by constraining the physical model with measurable parameters.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Conditions for runaway ruptures during reservoir operations: Magnitude–frequency distribution implications and application to Groningen

abstract: Precise control over nanoparticle composition and molecular architecture remains a fundamental challenge in nanomedicine, limiting systematic exploration of therapeutic design and biological function. Here, we report structurally defined protein spherical nucleic acids (ProSNAs) comprising ferritin nanocages densely functionalized with Toll-like receptor 9 (TLR9) agonist, immunostimulatory oligonucleotide shell for cancer immunotherapy. ProSNAs are rapidly internalized by immune cells, elicit potent innate immune activation, and exhibit prolonged intratumoral retention with preferential uptake by myeloid cells. These responses promote dendritic cell maturation, polarize macrophages toward an antitumor phenotype, and stimulate robust CD8 + T cell–mediated immunity. Across murine melanoma, colon adenocarcinoma, and triple-negative breast cancer models, a single intratumoral administration of ProSNAs induces durable tumor regression, suppresses metastatic progression, and synergizes with immune checkpoint blockade. Taken together, these findings establish ProSNAs as a structurally defined, myeloid-targeting nanomedicine platform for programmable cancer immunotherapy.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Protein spherical nucleic acids enable multivalent display of TLR9 agonists for enhanced cancer immunotherapy

abstract: Dynamic conformational changes of proteins are crucial for their cellular functions. Here we present a unified refinement pipeline for flexible protein structures in both CryoEM and in situ CryoET. Using a Gaussian mixture model–based focused alignment procedure, we improve resolution of small domains in highly dynamic proteins and reveal intricate conformational changes. The method corrects the per-subunit motion of TRPV1 and captures the rotary dynamics of ATP synthase within mitochondria.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Gaussian mixture model–based focused refinement for enhanced flexible structure determination in CryoEM and CryoET

abstract: The emergence of conspiracy theories in the wake of major events is a significant societal challenge. Here, we test whether conversational dialogues with a large language model (LLM) can reduce belief in immediately unfolding conspiracies. In experiments conducted in the days following the July 2024 assassination attempt on Donald Trump and the September 2025 assassination of Charlie Kirk, US adults (Experiment 1: N = 472; Experiment 2: N = 1,042) holding conspiratorial views about the crisis event engaged in a multiturn conversation with an LLM prompted to reduce their conspiracy belief. Compared to control participants who either discussed an irrelevant topic with an LLM or viewed a static fact sheet, participants in the LLM treatment showed significantly reduced conspiracy beliefs in both experiments. We also found suggestive evidence of downstream effects of the LLM treatment, observing reduced belief in some-but not all-analyses of different conspiratorial beliefs 1 to 2 mo later. These results shed light on the psychology of emerging conspiracies and highlight the potential for scalable, information-focused LLM interventions to counteract misinformation in the immediate aftermath of high-profile societal events.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Reducing belief in conspiracy theories as they unfold using large language models

abstract: Maternal inheritance of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) is thought to depend in part on elimination of paternal mtDNA during spermatogenesis, yet elevated sperm mtDNA copy number (mtDNAcn) is associated with reduced semen quality and longer time-to-pregnancy (TTP). Whether this reflects mtDNA retained within mature sperm or somatic-cell contamination remains unresolved. Here, we used digital PCR and an adapted mtDNA FISH in mature sperm among normospermic men in a prospective preconception pregnancy cohort. We directly visualized mtDNA in the sperm midpiece, and imaging-based mtDNA signal corresponded with bulk sperm mtDNAcn, supporting a sperm-intrinsic origin. Sperm mtDNA retention increased across mtDNAcn groups associated with lower fecundability, reflecting both higher proportion of mtDNA-positive sperm and greater midpiece signal. Substantial cell-to-cell heterogeneity suggests elevated bulk mtDNAcn reflects a distinct subpopulation of mtDNA-retaining sperm. These findings provide direct cellular evidence of mtDNA retention in a subset of mature human sperm and identify mtDNA retention as a sperm phenotype associated with lower fecundability despite normal semen parameters. More broadly, they refine current models of mitochondrial genome elimination during human spermatogenesis and provide cellular context for sperm mtDNAcn as a marker of fecundability.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Human sperm mitochondrial DNA retention is associated with reduced fecundability

abstract: Globally, 394,000 cases of Group B Streptococcus (GBS) infection occur each year, leading to significant morbidity and mortality. Vaccination has emerged as an important strategy to limit GBS infections and disease; however, existing vaccine candidates currently in clinical development do not cover all capsular polysaccharide serotypes. Here, we describe the use of a next generation bioconjugation platform to generate a decavalent GBS vaccine (GBS10V) and characterize its immunological evaluation in animals. Using an evolved PglS bioconjugation platform, capsular polysaccharides from all 10 GBS capsular polysaccharide serotypes were individually expressed and bioconjugated to an optimized Pseudomonas aeruginosa exotoxin A (EPA6) carrier protein engineered with six sequons. Multiple biochemical analyses confirmed the identity of each polysaccharide serotype bioconjugated to EPA6. Moreover, intact mass spectrometry (MS) and MS/MS spectra confirmed the presence of sialic acid in each repeat unit of GBS polysaccharides attached to the carrier, an attribute critical for eliciting an optimal immune response. The GBS10V vaccine was used to immunize outbred CD-1 mice and New Zealand White rabbits with doses of 1, 2, or 5 μg per GBS serotype. Sera analyses demonstrated the GBS10V vaccine induced high serotype-specific immunoglobulin titers to all 10 serotypes. Most importantly, interim and postimmune sera from rabbits demonstrated potent opsonophagocytic killing, with median titers ranging from 646 to 6,145 for all serotypes by day 42. Together, these findings establish GBS10V as a global GBS conjugate vaccine candidate for all patient populations, and thus, justify its further preclinical development.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: A decavalent Group B streptococcal biosynthetic conjugate vaccine provides functional immunity to all known serotypes

abstract: High-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) E7 proteins bind and inactivate host cellular tumor suppressors and are essential for the immortalization of primary human keratinocytes. E7 proteins from high- and low-risk HPV genotypes bind directly to at least two tumor suppressors, RB1 and PTPN14, and inactivate both. We previously characterized mutations in high-risk HPV E7 proteins that selectively abrogate the ability of E7 to bind either RB1 or PTPN14. Here, we established a genetic complementation system using the E7 mutants defective for binding to RB1 or PTPN14. Neither mutant alone could extend the lifespan of primary keratinocytes. When expressed together, the mutants could, like wild-type high-risk HPV E7, extend keratinocyte lifespan. Both high- and low-risk E7 reduced PTPN14 protein levels and reduced expression of keratinocyte differentiation genes, whereas only high-risk E7 reduced steady-state RB1 levels and induced E2F-dependent genes. Depletion of either RB1 or PTPN14 could cooperate with low-risk HPV6 E7 to extend keratinocyte lifespan. Our findings advance the model that inactivation of at least two tumor suppressors is required for the lifespan extension activity of high-risk HPV E7.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Inactivation of the RB1 and PTPN14 tumor suppressors cooperatively enables the lifespan extension activity of the human papillomavirus E7 oncoprotein

abstract: How development reliably generates complex patterns remains a central question in biology. Teeth provide an ideal system for addressing this problem, linking cusp-patterning mechanisms to diversification and the fossil record, yet the developmental basis of multicuspid crown patterning beyond mammals remains unresolved. In mammals, cusp initiation and spacing are controlled by transient epithelial signaling centers called enamel knots (EKs). Here, we combine comparative developmental analyses, 3D morphometrics, mutant perturbation, and Bayesian inverse modeling (BITES; Bayesian Inference for Tooth Emergence Simulation) to examine tooth morphogenesis across six squamate species representing convergent multicuspid dentitions. We find that cusp patterning in these taxa does not rely on a discrete EK-based patterning system. Instead, cusps arise from a broad, persistent cusp signaling field (CSF) that deploys canonical tooth-patterning pathways but lacks the spatial restriction, apoptosis, and discrete secondary EKs (SEKs) characteristic of the mammalian system. Changes in epithelial growth and signaling are associated with disproportionate expansion of this field during tooth development and with the formation of additional cusps. Quantitative variation in field extent and dynamics can generate crown morphologies within and across species, providing a developmental basis for positional heterodonty and repeated gains and losses of multicuspidity in squamates. Our results identify an alternative epithelial patterning architecture for vertebrate cusp formation, in which conserved tooth-patterning signals are deployed through a broad field-based architecture rather than compact signaling centers. Together, these findings revise how tooth developmental complexity is encoded and show how similar complex crown forms can evolve through distinct flexible epithelial patterning mechanisms.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: An alternative patterning mechanism for vertebrate tooth complexity

abstract: Cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) has revealed the structures of the ordered cores of amyloid fibrils assembled in vitro and isolated from diseased tissue. Many of the ex vivo amyloid structures contain low-resolution density adjacent to the protein core, often attributed to nonproteinaceous ligands, yet their identity has remained unresolved. Here, we characterize such density in distinct polymorphs of Aβ fibrils purified from the brains of homozygous App NL-F and App NL-G-F knock-in mouse models of Alzheimer’s disease. In App NL-G-F fibrils, which are built from the Arctic Aβ variant (E22G), we use immunogold labeling, immunofluorescence microscopy, and cryo-EM to identify the density as the glycosaminoglycans (GAGs) hyaluronic acid and chondroitin sulfate. These GAGs bind to an exposed positively charged patch on the Aβ 42 fibril surface, forming an intimate peptide-GAG copolymer through stacking interactions with the amyloid core.
