In App NL-F fibrils the predominant polymorph (~ 85% of particles) is glycan-free, with the relevant side chains identified in the App NL-G-F fibrils being buried within the App NL-F fibril core. Formation of the glycan-binding site in a rare polymorph hence involves conformational rearrangement to create the required binding surface. Our findings reveal a structural basis for GAG incorporation into brain-derived amyloid fibrils and highlight amyloid-associated ligands as potential therapeutic targets in protein aggregation disorders.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Glycosaminoglycans in the structures of Aβ 42 amyloid fibrils purified from mouse brains

abstract: Magnesium ions (Mg 2+) are vital for photosynthesis, serving as central metal ions in chlorophyll molecules and activating RuBisCO. MGT10 is the only member of the CorA/MRS2 superfamily bound to the chloroplast envelope membrane, where it mediates Mg 2+ uptake and homeostasis in chloroplasts. Despite its importance, the mechanism of MGT10-mediated Mg 2+ transport remains unclear. Here, we report cryoelectron microscopy structures of Arabidopsis MGT10 in two conformations, along with functional characterizations. MGT10 assembles into a homopentameric structure with a central tunnel connecting the transmembrane and soluble domains. A constriction ring consisting of five conserved arginine residues arranged asymmetrically in the tunnel is crucial for Mg 2+ conduction. Our structures reveal an unexpected gating mechanism involving a conformational transition from a symmetric closed state to an asymmetric, putatively open state. In addition, we identified an intramolecular disulfide bond within each soluble domain as a unique structural feature of MGT10. Structural and functional analyses show that this disulfide bond is required for MGT10’s structural integrity and for regulating its function in photosynthesis. Taken together, our findings provide insights into Mg 2+ transport and regulatory mechanisms of MGT10 in chloroplasts.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Structural basis of plastid Mg 2+ transport by the magnesium channel MGT10 in Arabidopsis

abstract: In 2025 the seasonal upwelling of the Gulf of Panama failed. Net primary production fell by 64% across the Gulf and industrial anchoveta landings dropped to 11% of the average, the lowest since the fishery became fully exploited in 1966. Anchoveta caught per purse-seine set fell to under a third of the normal rate while total catch per set stayed within its normal range. Landed fish carried about half their usual lipid content, and fish oil exports fell by 88% in both volume and value. The effects of one failed season reached international trade within months. Seasonal upwellings like this are common across the tropics yet far less studied than the large eastern boundary systems. The very strong El Niño now under way makes the 2027 season more uncertain.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Failure of a tropical upwelling rapidly collapsed Panama’s anchoveta fishery and its exports

abstract: Faithful transmission of chromatin states through cell division requires symmetric transfer of parental histones to daughter strands, yet the underlying mechanisms remain elusive. Here, we identify the replisome scaffold Ctf4 as a bona fide histone chaperone that directly orchestrates parental histone transfer to preserve epigenetic inheritance. We show that the N-terminal domain (NTD) of Ctf4 harbors a specific histone-binding motif (HBM) embedded within its intrinsically disordered linker region. This HBM engages the DNA-binding surface of histone H3 and, in concert with Spt16 and Mcm2, transiently tethers parental histone hexamer onto Tof1 at the advancing replisome, priming them for subsequent transfer to nascent DNA. Disrupting Ctf4-HBM severely compromises parental histone sequestration, misdirects their recycling away from the lagging strand, and causes substantial loss of gene silencing at heterochromatic loci. Our findings establish Ctf4 not merely as a structural scaffold, but as a central chaperone at the replication fork that actively governs symmetric partitioning of parental histones, thereby ensuring the fidelity of epigenetic memory through successive cell divisions.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Ctf4 chaperones parental histones to preserve epigenetic memory

abstract: Biological phosphorus (P) mobilization is generally attributed to proton- and ligand-driven dissolution of mineral P, enzymatic hydrolysis of organic P, and, under anoxic conditions, reductive release of phosphate from Fe(III) minerals. Here, we show that extracellular metabolites released by diverse Gram-positive bacteria sustain Fe(III) reduction under oxic conditions, releasing mineral-associated phosphate. The resulting Fe(II) reacts with O 2 to generate reactive oxygen species that activate organic P. This redox pathway was observed across diverse aerobic bacteria and agricultural soils and increased plant-available P. These findings establish aerobic microbial Fe redox chemistry as a previously overlooked route for returning otherwise inaccessible P to bioavailable pools, with implications for reactivating legacy P in agricultural soils.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
journal_ref: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
title: Microbially driven iron redox chemistry unlocks phosphorus reservoirs in oxygenated soils

abstract: Symmetries shape the quantum-information dynamics of many-body systems, but their effect on nonstabilizerness, the resource complementary to entanglement, is less understood. We compute the stabilizer Renyi entropy, a measure of nonstabilizerness, in U(1)-symmetric one-dimensional random circuits. The disorder-averaged dynamics is captured by a four-replica tensor network, which we evaluate by S4-adapted infinite time-evolving block decimation (iTEBD) directly in the thermodynamic limit. Together with a hydrodynamic argument, our results identify a diffusive universality class for the late-time approach of nonstabilizerness to its random-state value, with the stabilizer Renyi entropy gap closing as 1/t. The same scaling is verified in an energy-conserving nonintegrable Ising chain. More broadly, our framework provides a hydrodynamic perspective on nonstabilizerness generation and offers insight into the design of approximate Haar-random states in Hamiltonian dynamics.
journal: Physical Review Letters
journal_ref: Physical Review Letters
title: Diffusive Dynamics of Nonstabilizerness

abstract: We develop a nonadiabatic theory of phonon magnetic moments applicable to both insulators and metals. By relating the phonon magnetic moment to the force-velocity response of ions in a magnetic field, we derive a gauge-invariant expression using a gauge-covariant Wigner expansion. The formalism naturally separates Fermi-sea and Fermi-surface contributions and captures the full dependence on phonon frequency. In gapped systems, our theory reduces to previous adiabatic expressions in the low-frequency limit. Beyond this limit, it reveals additional contributions arising from resonant interband processes and the Fermi surface. Applying our theory to Pb 1 − x Sn x Te, we find that the Fermi-surface contribution substantially enhances the phonon magnetic moment, reproducing the same order of magnitude as the experimental observation. Our results provide a unified framework for describing phonon magnetic moments beyond the adiabatic regime.
journal: Physical Review Letters
journal_ref: Physical Review Letters
title: Nonadiabatic theory of phonon magnetic moments in insulators and metals

abstract: Inertial confinement fusion (ICF) experiments at the National Ignition Facility (NIF) use high-density carbon shells doped with low-concentration tungsten in a thin, uniform-density, buried layer, to suppress deleterious high-energy x-ray pre-heating. Recent radiation-hydrodynamics simulations suggest that this boxcar dopant-concentration profile causes hydrodynamically unstable density gradients leading to fuel-shell mixing and up to 2× degraded neutron yields. To address this, a new ramped profile was tested, where the dopant concentration linearly ramps up and back down. Two NIF experiments using this strategy demonstrated neutron yield improvements of up to 2.2× over the closest boxcar comparison, achieving a record 8.6 MJ yield, 20.1 keV hot-spot temperature, and a target gain of 4.1. These results show that ramped doping is consistent with mitigation of fuel-ablator mixing and marks a key development for ICF science.
journal: Physical Review Letters
journal_ref: Physical Review Letters
title: Improved Fusion Yields at the National Ignition Facility via Ramped-Profile Capsule Doping

abstract: The computational discovery of phonon-mediated superconductors is hindered by the prohibitive cost of density functional perturbation theory (DFPT). Here, guided by the metallized σ -bonding picture, we introduce the σ -bonding density of states ( σ DOS) as an efficient physical descriptor to identify high-transition-temperature ( T c ) superconductors from density functional theory (DFT)-level electronic structure without explicit DFPT calculations. The evaluation of σ DOS can be further accelerated by a deep-learning DFT Hamiltonian method, enabling efficient large-scale screening for phonon-mediated superconductors. Screening 2 million materials, we identify B 13 Se as an ambient-pressure superconductor candidate with predicted T c > 40 ~K, together with a family of high- T c B 13 X candidates, supporting the effectiveness of this discovery strategy. By bridging physics priors with AI acceleration, this study delivers an efficient and generalizable route for computational materials discovery in the AI era.
journal: Physical Review Letters
journal_ref: Physical Review Letters
title: AI-accelerated metallized σ -bonding screening for discovering phonon-mediated superconductors

abstract: Niobium holds a pivotal place in superconductivity history: it is not only the elemental superconductor with the highest critical temperature, but also a long-standing candidate for multiband pairing whose evidence has remained controversial. A two-gap scenario was proposed as early as 1959, yet experimental proof stayed elusive. Here, through thermal Hall effect measurements, we unambiguously demonstrate a crossover in transverse thermal transport below $T_{\rm c}$ , where the dominant carrier switches from hole-like to electron-like upon cooling. This crossover is a clear hallmark of two distinct superconducting condensates. Fitting our data to a two-gap Bardeen-Rickayzen-Tewordt (BRT) model yields a second energy gap of approximately 0.22 $k_{\rm B}T_{\rm c}$ , only 11% of the dominant gap. This small gap size accounts for the difficulty in resolving the two-gap structure in earlier experiments. Crucially, the temperature at which the electron-like contribution to longitudinal thermal conductivity begins to dominate coincides with the temperature at which the thermal Hall angle per unit field starts to decrease upon cooling at low field, confirming consistency between the two methods, and providing crucial information on the assignment of the superconducting gaps to their respective hole- or electron-like Fermi surface sheets. These findings not only resolve a longstanding controversy, but also establish that multigap superconductivity is far more common than previously assumed, and demonstrate the thermal Hall effect as a powerful probe for resolving gap multiplicities in superconductors.
journal: Physical Review Letters
journal_ref: Physical Review Letters
title: Thermal Hall effect in elemental niobium, a two-gap superconductor

abstract: We present a wave equation for surface plasmon polaritons on smooth and macroscopically curved metal-dielectric interfaces of arbitrary shape. It features two terms linear in curvature: an isotropic geometric potential, defining an effective refractive-index landscape, and an anisotropic operator, making the index propagation-axis dependent. This birefringence vanishes if the metal-to-dielectric permittivity ratio equals minus the golden ratio squared. Applying our equation to quantum emitters on metal spherical patches, we show that curvature reshapes plasmon-mediated collective decay rates and frequency shifts.
journal: Physical Review Letters
journal_ref: Physical Review Letters
title: Birefringent curvature control of surface plasmons and collective emission

abstract: We introduce a systematic framework to construct nonlocal observables with extensive quantum Fisher information (QFI) density in stabilizer codes. The construction maps stabilizer generators to dual Ising spins whose correlators equal string order parameters, converting hidden nonlocal order into a possibly metrologically accessible observable. Applying this to monitored cluster codes and the toric code, we identify transitions in the QFI scaling from an extensive regime—where long-range string order prevails—to an intensive one driven by competing single-site measurements.
journal: Physical Review Letters
journal_ref: Physical Review Letters
title: Assembling extensive quantum Fisher information in stabilizer systems

abstract: Nonlinear optical interactions are typically driven by coherent sources. Recently, however, incoherent sources have also been shown to offer new opportunities in nonlinear optics. Here we study the effects of the source incoherence in second harmonic generation. We derive and experimentally validate an analytic expression for the far-field coherence function at the second harmonic frequency, which is a generalization of the well-known van Cittert-Zernike theorem. Unlike the linear optics case, here the results depend not only on the source spatial distribution, but also on the nonlinear structure of the crystal. We further show, by performing Young's double-slit measurement, that the coherence at the second harmonic increases as the light propagates inside the nonlinear crystal. Our results establish nonlinearity as a degree of freedom for optical coherence, opening a new research area at the interface of statistical optics and nonlinear optics.
journal: Physical Review Letters
journal_ref: Physical Review Letters
title: Van Cittert–Zernike theorem in nonlinear wave mixing

abstract: Are Gaussian measurements enough to distinguish between Gaussian states? Here, we tackle this question by focusing on the max-relative entropy as an operational distinguishability metric. Given two multimode Gaussian states ρ , σ with covariance matrices V σ > V ρ , we derive a condition that completely determines whether or not there exists an optimal Gaussian measurement achieving the max-relative entropy. When the condition is satisfied, we find this optimal measurement explicitly. When the condition is not met, there is a strict gap between the distinguishability achievable by Gaussian measurements and the unconstrained max-relative entropy in which all measurements are allowed. We illustrate our results in the single-mode setting, and show examples of states for which this gap can be made arbitrarily large, revealing novel instances of Gaussian data hiding.
journal: Physical Review Letters
journal_ref: Physical Review Letters
title: Optimal discrimination of Gaussian states by Gaussian measurements

abstract: We construct Pulsar Polarisation Arrays (PPA), using regular pulsars monitored in MeerKAT’s Thousand Pulsar Array (TPA) Programme, to search for Axion-like Dark Matter (ALDM) within Milky Way. Specifically, from a catalogue of 1237 regular pulsars, we select the 50 ones with the highest signal-to-noise ratio and set upper limits on the ALDM Chern-Simons coupling. We find no signals with statistical significance over the mass range of [ 10 − 23 , 10 − 20 ] e V in the six-year MeerKAT’s data. By combining the high-quality TPA pulsars and the accurate ionospheric subtraction of , we establish the most sensitive upper limits to the date on the ALDM Chern-Simons coupling, namely ≲ 10 − 14 − 3 × 10 − 13 GeV − 1 , for the mass range of [ 10 − 23 , 10 − 21 ] e V except at m a ≃ 1.3 × 10 − 22 eV. This study highlights the great promise of regular-pulsar PPAs, whose large population and flexible design open a powerful new window on fundamental physics with next-generation radio telescopes.
journal: Physical Review Letters
journal_ref: Physical Review Letters
title: MeerKAT thousand-pulsar polarization array: Searches for ultralight axionlike dark matter

abstract: Magnetoelectric multiferroic composites, which combine ferroelectric and ferromagnetic phases, are pivotal for next-generation electronic devices. Conventional design strategies prioritize ferroelectric materials with large spontaneous polarization to achieve strong magnetoelectric coupling. Here, we propose a paradigm-shifting approach that instead utilizes a material’s high strain sensitivity of polarization. The quantum paraelectric SrTiO3 is discovered as an ideal ferroelectric component due to its exceptionally high polarization response to strain, far exceeding that of classical ferroelectrics like BaTiO3 or PbTiO3. To demonstrate this concept, the desired SrTiO3-NiO nanocomposite films featuring ordered nanopillar array and atomically sharp vertical interfaces were fabricated. This nanostructure maximizes the interfacial contact area and ensures highly efficient strain transfer. The resulting composite exhibits a giant direct magnetoelectric coupling coefficient of 3200 mV/(cm·Oe) at room temperature, demonstrating a remarkably strong macroscopic magnetoelectric response compared with conventional 1-3 composite oxide multiferroic systems. Through a combination of atomic-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy and first-principles calculations, we reveal the outstanding performance originates from the unique strain-sensitive polarization of SrTiO3, which can effectively trigger substantial polarization variations via magnetic field-induced strain transfer across coherent interface. This work redefines the design principle for high-performance magnetoelectric composites by emphasizing strain sensitivity over large polarization, opening a new pathway for developing ultra-sensitive sensors and multi-state, low-power memory devices.
journal: Physical Review Letters
journal_ref: Physical Review Letters
title: Giant Room-Temperature Magnetoelectric Coupling Effect in Nanocomposite Thin Films via Strain-Sensitive Polarization

abstract: Ordered crystals generally exhibit crystalline heat transport, even when a boson peak is present. Here we show that the quasi-one-dimensional single crystal ( N b 4 S e 15 I 2 ) I 2 exhibits ultralow, glass-like thermal transport: its thermal conductivity increases monotonically and reaches only 0.21 W m − 1 K − 1 at 20 K. Heat-capacity and low-frequency Raman measurements reveal a boson-peak-like excess of low-energy vibrational states. The crystal consists of a rigid phonon-carrying backbone and weakly coordinated interchain I − ions. \blue{Ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) reveals unusually large, strongly anisotropic, and anharmonic motion of these ions, while phonon calculations show an avoided crossing between low-frequency optical and acoustic branches, establishing acoustic–optical hybridization. Structural and AIMD evidence supports substantial involvement of the interchain subsystem in the soft low-frequency modes. A minimal theory shows how hybridization with strongly anharmonic interchain dynamics can reduce the group velocity and lifetime of acoustic-like heat carriers. These results link the boson-peak-like excess and glass-like heat transport as related but distinct consequences of coupling between a rigid heat-carrying backbone and weakly coordinated interchain degrees of freedom, suggesting a structural route to anomalous heat transport in ordered low-dimensional crystals.
journal: Physical Review Letters
journal_ref: Physical Review Letters
title: Glassy heat transport from interchain rattling in an ordered quasi-one-dimensional crystal

abstract: It is challenging to build scalable quantum processors capable of both parallel control and local operation. As a promising platform to overcome this challenge, optical lattices offer exceptional parallelism. However, it has been struggling with precise local operations due to relatively narrow lattice spacings. Here, we introduce a new quantum processor incorporating orbit-qubit encoding and internal states (as auxiliary degrees of freedom) to achieve spatially selective operations together with parallel control. With this processor, we generate one-dimensional and two-dimensional cluster states using minimal layers of controlled-Z gates. We experimentally detect the multipartite entanglement of a two-dimensional cluster state involving 123 orbit qubits through direct stabilizer measurements, verifying the full bipartite non-separability. Furthermore, we demonstrate measurement-based quantum computation by implementing single-qubit and two-qubit logical gates, highlighting the flexibility of orbit-qubit operations. Our results establish orbit-qubit optical lattices as a scalable quantum processing architecture, opening new pathways for quantum computation applications.
journal: Physical Review Letters
journal_ref: Physical Review Letters
title: Orbit-Qubit Quantum Processor of Ultracold Atoms

abstract: Acoustic plasmons, collective charge excitations exhibiting a linear, sound-like dispersion, have long eluded experimental identification in bulk materials. The layered correlated metal Sr2RuO4 hosts two distinct types of acoustic plasmons. Here, we show that, beyond the conventional picture, the low-energy acoustic plasmon arises from a two-component carrier separation that is driven by short-range Coulomb interactions associated with crystal local field effects (LFE). The high-energy acoustic plasmon branches, well captured inside the first Brillouin zone by a layered-electron-gas model with weak interlayer hopping, also reappear periodically in higher zones thanks to LFE. Our ab initio calculations agree well with existing experimental spectra, reconciling prior conflicting interpretations, without the need of invoking strong electronic correlation effects at play in Sr2RuO4.
journal: Physical Review Letters
journal_ref: Physical Review Letters
title: Two types of acoustic plasmons in Sr 2 RuO 4 driven by short-range Coulomb interactions

abstract: Recently, a distinct component of black hole binary merger radiation, named the direct wave, has been identified. The frequency and damping time of the direct wave have been associated with properties of the remnant horizon. This has led to direct wave based analysis of GW250114, including a test of Hawking’s area law. However, as we demonstrate here for comparable mass binaries using numerical relativity strain data, the direct wave frequency is not correlated with the horizon frequency or surface gravity, other than an incidental crossing around χ f ≈ 0.7 corresponding closely to the remnant spin of GW250114. Because the damping time shows significant evolution a single damped sinusoid model with a fixed damping time is not appropriate to model the entire direct wave, except for short time intervals. We further show that an evolving frequency model based on horizon properties also does not model the direct wave component for systems with large remnant spins. We demonstrate that testing Hawking’s area law with a horizon frequency based on the direct wave interpretation may lead to apparent violations of Hawking’s area law when no violation actually occurs. Our results therefore indicate that the direct wave is not a reliable probe of the remnant horizon’s properties for comparable mass mergers.
journal: Physical Review Letters
journal_ref: Physical Review Letters
title: Direct wave is not a meaningful test of horizon properties

abstract: Observing non-Gaussianities in the timing residuals of pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) has recently attracted attention as a potential discriminator between astrophysical and cosmological origins of the observed gravitational wave (GW) signal. In this Letter, we show that, even in an idealized signal-dominated setup, after decorrelating the data to avoid spurious detections, statistical tests applied to PTA data cannot distinguish between a Gaussian and a non-Gaussian amplitude distribution of the GW background in a model-agnostic way. In particular, without making strong assumptions on the GW spectrum or the properties of the population, the sensitivity to any distinctive non-Gaussian feature is washed out.
journal: Physical Review Letters
journal_ref: Physical Review Letters
title: Are Pulsar Timing Array Measurements Sensitive to Gravitational Wave Non-Gaussianities?

abstract: Topological semimetals host band nodes characterized by quantized invariants that can appear in bulk responses, yet some invariants remain hidden from standard probes. In particular, band nodes can carry secondary topological charges whose transport signatures are still largely unexplored. Here we study three-dimensional nodal-line semimetals in which nodal rings carry both the Berry phase w 1 π and a ℤ 2 monopole charge w 2 . We show that magnetic quantum oscillations, usually treated as a probe of w 1 , can directly diagnose w 2 of an isolated nodal ring whose torus hole contains no other Fermi surface, with the relevant signal selected by the magnetic-field direction. For a field along the ring axis, the inner and outer extremal orbits of the toroidal Fermi surface both encircle the w 2 -enforced thread and exhibit a topological phase shift ν w 2 π in the ν th harmonic, which is accessible through standard phase-resolved quantum-oscillation analysis. By contrast, for a field applied perpendicular to the ring axis, the relevant extremal orbit exhibits the usual π phase shift associated with the Berry phase w 1 π , independent of w 2 . For weak doping, three-dimensional ABC-stacked graphdiyne is predicted to exhibit the proposed oscillations in a field range accessible with present-day high-field facilities.
journal: Physical Review Letters
journal_ref: Physical Review Letters
title: Quantum oscillation signatures of 𝒵 2 monopole charge in nodal-ring semimetals

abstract: Understanding how angular momentum is exchanged between different degrees of freedom has long been a subject of fundamental interest, as represented by the Einstein-de Haas effect in a ferromagnet, in which a change of rotational speed of the rigid body is induced by a change of magnetization. Here, we report the imprinting of orbital angular momentum (OAM) of light to a superconductor, a macroscopic quantum state of fermionic condensate, through the Higgs mode excitation by a terahertz (THz) vortex beam. By using spatiotemporally resolved THz-pump and THz-probe spectroscopy, we observe a rotating order parameter oscillation in which the phase structure of the vortex beam is imprinted onto the Higgs mode. Time-dependent Ginzburg–Landau analysis shows that the rotating Higgs mode carries a finite OAM. This work opens a pathway for imprinting OAM of light onto a superconductor and manipulating its order parameter.
journal: Physical Review Letters
journal_ref: Physical Review Letters
title: Imprinting Macroscopic Orbital Angular Momentum onto the Superconducting Higgs Mode Using a Terahertz Vortex Beam

abstract: ${\rm{EuTe}}_{4}$ is a polar charge density wave (CDW) material, with giant thermal hysteresis and non-volatile state switching under electric and optical fields, attracting great attention in recent years. However, the in-depth understanding of these anomalous phenomena remains elusive. Herein, via first-principles calculations, we reveal that the polar CDW state in ${\rm{EuTe}}_{4}$ hosts a novel layer-selective nature, wherein multiple energetically close CDW configurations coexist and exhibit low interconversion energy barriers. Monte Carlo simulations indicate that the giant thermal hysteresis in ${\rm{EuTe}}_{4}$ originates from a configurational-entropy-driven crossover between ordered and disordered states, around which the material hosts a metastable CDW state characterized by diverse local polar configurations breaking the out-of-plane translational symmetry. The configurational composition of this metastable CDW state can be effectively controlled by electric and optical fields, thereby enabling non-volatile state switching. Our theoretical findings align well with recent experimental observations in ${\rm{EuTe}}_{4}$ and pave the way for exploring the emerging phenomena and applications of polar CDW in multilayered systems.
journal: Physical Review Letters
journal_ref: Physical Review Letters
title: Multiple layer-selective polar charge density waves in EuTe 4

abstract: In neutron star (NS) magnetospheres, plasma waves propagate as normal modes with distinct propagation dynamics that strongly influence observable signals. This letter presents a unified theory of linear mode conversion between Alfvén (A), superluminal ordinary (O), and extraordinary (X) modes, incorporating the effect of magnetic-field geometry and local plasma response. Within this framework, we show that magnetic field-line curvature induces A–X conversion for waves and O–X conversion at high frequencies, whereas plasma gradients alone do not drive X-mode coupling. A single dimensionless parameter, Δ , controls both conversion channels. The coupled mode equations for these two channels resemble nonadiabatic transitions in multilevel quantum systems and admit an exact solution in terms of triconfluent Heun functions. The conversion efficiency is a universal function of Δ and peaks at about 49%. Our analysis further demonstrates that efficient conversion occurs within a narrow angular window between the wave vector and magnetic field, localizing potential conversion sites in the NS magnetosphere. We suggest that this linear mechanism may account for orthogonally polarized modes in pulsars, and possibly for similar polarization features in other radio transients.
journal: Physical Review Letters
journal_ref: Physical Review Letters
title: Linear mode conversion in ultramagnetized pair plasmas: Single-parameter scaling

abstract: Relaxation in an interacting system is determined not only by its initial distance from equilibrium, but also by the relaxation modes populated by the initial state. Here we experimentally observe and control the Mpemba effect, in which a state farther from equilibrium overtakes one initially closer, in an extended, disordered 13C nuclear-spin network in diamond. Field cycling allows us to prepare distinct spatial polarization profiles by independently controlling hyperpolarization and defect-mediated relaxation. We then track their evolution under Floquet driving, which stabilizes a long-lived prethermal regime. We observe reproducible Mpemba crossings and tune the crossing time over several orders of magnitude, from late-time thermalization into the prethermal plateau. Semiclassical simulations show that randomly positioned paramagnetic defects create fast-relaxing regions and defect-poor regions that support the slowest collective relaxation mode. The Mpemba crossings are set by the initial state overlap with this mode. Our results demonstrate anomalous relaxation within a prethermal many-body regime and identify disorder, transport, and mode-selective state preparation as resources for controlling relaxation in extended spin networks.
journal: Physical Review Letters
journal_ref: Physical Review Letters
title: Tunable Mpemba effect in a prethermal many-body spin network

abstract: The quantum anomalous Hall (QAH) effect exhibits one-way chiral edge states at zero external magnetic field, which so far relies primarily on nonzero out-of-plane ferromagnetic (FM) responses. Despite theoretical predictions, experimental implementation of antiferromagnetic (AFM) QAH materials remains lacking. Here, we report the first observation of gapped photonic AFM QAH phases with nonzero Chern numbers and net-zero magnetizations in the microwave regime, using two-dimensional magneto-optical photonic crystals made from paired ferrites with equal but opposite magnetizations and intermediate anisotropic couplings. The combined effect of AFM order, time-reversal symmetry breaking, and crystalline symmetry breaking generates the topological bulk band gap. The sign of the Chern number, associated with the chirality of edge states, can be easily switched by rotating copper stripes to change coupling orientations, rather than flipping magnetizations. Our work paves the way for exploring new programmable, AFM-based topological photonic functional devices that may be absent in FM ones.
journal: Physical Review Letters
journal_ref: Physical Review Letters
title: Photonic antiferromagnetic quantum anomalous Hall effect with switchable chirality of edge states

abstract: A search for the e + e − → f 1 ( 1285 ) reaction is performed with the CMD-3 detector at the VEPP-2000 collider. Data from a scan in the center-of-mass energy range E_{c.m.}=1.20–1.36 GeV with 109.1 pb − 1 of the integrated luminosity is used. A dedicated 51.7 pb − 1 have been collected at the f 1 ( 1285 ) resonance peak energy E_{c.m.}=1282 MeV, where 26.5 ± 7.4 events have been found in the e + e − → η π 0 π 0 reaction. No indication of the signal is observed in the non-resonant scan data. We interpret the result as statistical 4.5 σ evidence of the C-even resonance production in the e + e − → f 1 ( 1285 ) → η π 0 π 0 reaction via the two-photon interaction. The production cross section is found to be $\sigma(\epem\to f_1) = 0.074 \pm 0.021 \pm 0.010$ nb, and the corresponding branching fraction to the e + e − pair is $B(f_1(1285)\to\epem) = (8.3 \pm 2.3 \pm 1.1)\times 10^{-9}$ .
journal: Physical Review Letters
journal_ref: Physical Review Letters
title: Evidence of the e + e − → f 1 (1285) reaction with the CMD-3 detector at VEPP-2000

abstract: Direct evidence of exciton condensation in semiconductor heterostructures remains elusive. Here we propose charge transport of doped carriers as a probe of exciton condensation in transition-metal dichalcogenide heterostructures and identify distinct experimental signatures. First, condensation suppresses the phase space for carrier scattering, leading to a reduction in resistivity, that provides a general diagnostic of exciton condensation. Second, in heterostructures with a tunable solid-state Feshbach resonance, condensate-induced hybridization between doped carriers and trion bound states qualitatively modifies transport. In particular, near resonance, this hybridization yields an effective inverted cyclotron motion and a corresponding sign reversal of the Hall resistivity. These results establish charge transport as a promising route for detecting and characterizing exciton condensation in semiconductor heterostructures.
journal: Physical Review Letters
journal_ref: Physical Review Letters
title: Detecting exciton condensation through charge transport in semiconductor heterostructures

abstract: Signatures of a material object’s broken inversion symmetry within its intrinsic excitations and associated optical fields have largely evaded characterization from a perspective that evenly accounts for the inseparability between matter and field dynamics. Here, we formulate a complex-valued pseudoscalar chirality metric that is derived from the coupled electromagnetic and material governing equations, and demonstrate its resolution of the excitational chirality exhibited by the eigenmodes and eigenfields of a family of structurally chiral objects, including those with chirally connected enantiomeric states.
journal: Physical Review Letters
journal_ref: Physical Review Letters
title: Unified light-matter metric of molecular and nanophotonic chirality

abstract: Solving for the motion of spinning test particles in curved spacetimes is important for modeling gravitational-wave inspirals of spinning compact binaries. We build a Hamiltonian formalism in worldline-adapted frames for the spinning test particle and formulate a corresponding Hamilton-Jacobi equation valid to linear order in spin. We prove that when the geodesic motion in a spacetime and the parallel transport along said geodesics are both separable, then so is the corresponding Hamilton-Jacobi equation. The key insight is that the transform to the worldline-adapted frame that separates parallel transport also coincidentally generates a near-identity transform into separation coordinates in the orbital sector. We illustrate this in black hole, plane wave, and cosmological spacetimes.
journal: Physical Review Letters
journal_ref: Physical Review Letters
title: Separability of the motion of spinning test particles in curved space-time

abstract: A novel paradigm for sorting is introduced, based upon resetting. Using simple examples, we demonstrate that sorting is achieved by resetting the velocity component(s) or orientation of the particles, rather than position. The objects to be sorted are microparticles, modeled as suspended and spatially extended Brownian particles. This sorting-by-resetting scheme illustrates that stochastic resetting can create non-equilibrium conditions which enable tasks forbidden at thermodynamic equilibrium.
journal: Physical Review Letters
journal_ref: Physical Review Letters
title: Sorting by resetting

abstract: Co-based protonic ceramic fuel cells (PCFCs) demonstrate promising energy conversion at intermediate temperatures (400–650 °C), their practical application is limited by transport kinetics and chemical incompatibility at the electrode–electrolyte interface. These limitations are primarily governed by the spin state of the cobalt ions. Our temperature dependent K β emission spectra show that Co 3 + ion in the BaCo 0.4 Fe 0.4 Zr 0.1 Y 0.1 O 3 − δ (BCFZY) electrode exhibit a predominantly HS state post-irradiation, whereas it remains in a predominantly LS state up to 600 °C prior to irradiation. This spin-state transition alleviates associated with the LS Co 3 + /IS Co 4 + pathway, which otherwise limits charge transport, thus boosting PCFCs performance. Post-irradiation, the power density increased from 1.14 to 1.84 W·cm − 2 , accompanied by an ultralow degradation rate of 0.0077% h − 1 during a 1,250-hour durability test. Improved stability is attributed to the HS Co 3 + ions’ large ionic radius, which facilitates lattice expansion and enhances interfacial compatibility. This work establishes a novel spin-state-based strategy for advancing PCFCs performance.
journal: Physical Review Letters
journal_ref: Physical Review Letters
title: Lifting the spin-blockade effect in Co-based electrode to boost fuel cell performance

abstract: Clean, nonsplit vortex zero-bias peaks (ZBPs) can be misinterpreted as Majorana zero modes (MZMs), making static scanning tunneling microscopy intrinsically ambiguous. Here we use the STM tip coupling to drive a local boundary-renormalization-group (boundary RG) flow, turning dynamical Coulomb blockade into a falsification test for Majorana-like ZBPs. Experimentally, in a SrSn3 thin film, normal-state spectra establish an Ohmic dissipative environment, and a common boundary-RG/thermodynamic-Bethe-ansatz analysis of the superconducting-gap and vortex-center spectra yields consistent dissipation strengths within the r < 1/2 Majorana-filter regime. Lowering the tip nevertheless drives a clean, non-split vortex-center ZBP into a zero-bias dip, opposite to the protected flow of an isolated MZM, unmasking the peak as a Majorana false positive produced by a conventional vortex-core state. The same flow selectively suppresses the strongly tip-coupled channel, resolving the two-gap superconductivity. Dissipative STM thus tests dynamical protection rather than spectral appearance.

abstract: Atom probe tomography (APT) provides three-dimensional compositional maps at near-atomic resolution, but its accuracy is limited by the dynamics of field evaporation. Here we show that ion emission in APT occurs in intermittent bursts with strong spatiotemporal correlations. High-field atoms act as pinning sites whose depinning triggers avalanches of evaporation. These cascades extend up to 10 3 evaporated atoms and display dynamics consistent with Hawkes processes. A minimal branching-process model captures the burst statistics, while simulations of a binary alloy reveal logarithmic kinetic roughening of the evaporation front, consistent with extremal depinning in two dimensions with long-range elasticity. These results demonstrate that field evaporation is governed by avalanche dynamics with universal features, calling for a fundamental revision of APT reconstruction methods.

abstract: We propose an interacting model that is exactly solvable in any spatial dimension and gives rise to a Fermi liquid (FL) featuring a pseudogapped (PG) single-particle spectral function and a vanishing quasiparticle (QP) weight at half-filling, without invoking Mott physics. The PG originates from a purely fermionic mechanism through emergent QPs arising from a correlated hopping interaction. By employing an appropriate coherent-state basis, we derive a Gaussian path-integral representation of the partition function, which enables systematic treatments of deviations from the Gaussian limit using standard many-body techniques, such as diagrammatic perturbation theory or mean-field theory. We explicitly demonstrate and discuss several properties of the exactly solvable limit on the square lattice, including the mechanism for temperature-dependent PG opening, the singular behavior of the self-energy, the violation of the Luttinger sum rule, and the role of Luttinger and Fermi surfaces. Finally, we explore quantum phase transitions between PG-FLs and Landau FLs.
